verdict.rationale: TypeSafe publishes a dedicated vendor-authored 'model jaggedness' page for jev-1.13 listing nine specific failure modes (literal reading, math/counting, date-time comparison, indirection, large irrelevant state, adversarial content, contradictory instructions, structural invariants, generation) each paired with a 'Do this instead' mitigation, dated and versioned. Community testing (jev-comm-7, jev-comm-9) surfaces additional real-world jaggedness (order-sensitivity, confidence being a derived formula) that isn't explicitly named on the vendor's list, showing the documented list isn't fully exhaustive. Missing for 10: the vendor page doesn't address the specific choice-ordering sensitivity or confidence-metric critique raised independently, and there's no first-party benchmark quantifying failure rates.
